title: Monthly residual sea-level scale had no clear pooled change at 101 gauges from 1960-1989 to 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether monthly mean relative sea-level scale changed between 1960-1989 and 1995-2024 after removal of separate trends and seasonal cycles. We used a fixed PSMSL RLR archive and 101 gauges with at least 95% accepted months in both periods. The primary model removed a linear trend and calendar-month effects in each period. Equal weight for 33 occupied 10-degree cells gave a geometric mean residual-scale change of -3.60%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -10.06% to +3.20%. Each of 4,999 draws resampled years jointly across sites and refitted the models. Equal-gauge weighting gave -2.18%, with limits -7.84% to +4.79%. Quadratic detrending, one- and five-year blocks, and stricter missing-data checks also left the sign uncertain. Scale rose at 45 sites and fell at 56 sites as point estimates. The evidence does not resolve a common increase or decrease in this sample. It does not prove constant variability, establish a physical cause, or measure flood risk. Sparse southern coverage, climate dependence beyond the blocks, independent period resampling, site changes, and source revisions limit inference. The package includes input rows, source hashes, selection evidence, site and cell results, all pooled draws, code, a figure, an independent formula and source audit, and an offline repeat.

display.caption: Residual monthly scale had no clear pooled change between the two periods. Panel A shows station changes, with colors capped at -35% and +35%. Panel B gives equal-cell summaries and conditional 95% three-year block intervals with model refits. The zero-missing-day check uses 64 gauges in 24 cells; other displayed fits use 101 gauges in 33 cells. Panel C compares primary residual scales. None of these measures is a global ocean average or a flood-risk estimate.
